answer: Each agent splices one copper cable run and locks a 70-credit bond. It crimps a pearl bead with a unique serial into the joint and seals the joint with sable dye. A random peer re-tests the splice for continuity and co-signs the bead serial in the registry, marking it consumed. The splice fee is 35 for the first run, 35+6(k-1) for the k-th; the 1000th costs 6029, so 1000 fakes pay 3,032,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-splice ring fails: one bead cannot seal two splices, and a copied serial burns both bonds. An honest splicer pays 35 once and redeems the bond after a clean epoch.
